correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and kappa>0, the sampled Fourier multiplier f=(A+B cos theta)/D^2 is strictly positive by alias positivity; B>0 because a>tanh a and A>B by endpoints. Polynomial division gives W+V cos theta+R/(A+B cos theta), whose geometric Fourier coefficients periodize exactly. For distances >=2 positivity of the wrapped geometric pair gives strict alternating signs. The n-even nearest-neighbor inequality Rt/s>V/2 and n-odd monotone comparison to the negative three-site inverse prove the remaining signs. The norm bound is a geometric tail, order-one control a degree-one inverse. The standalone arbitrary-precision checker passed 14980 direct covariance and Fourier checks plus the order-one control; finite checks corroborate rather than prove the theorem.

value.rationale: Exact zero vs nonzero entries of a Gaussian precision matrix determine conditional independence, so establishing that every point-sampled order-two circular Matérn process has a complete signed dependence graph—unlike exactly nearest-neighbor order one—is a natural structural and statistical question. The explicit exponentially decaying finite-grid truncation error quantifies when sparse numerical approximations remain useful. The full all-grid, all-parameter statement is not a textbook normalization identity, finite anecdote, or arbitrary parameter slice.
